current.text: He signed with Minnesota and is reported to be starting for the Wolves.
He was reportedly promised a starting spot, but that spot may not last all season.
He should get more minutes and chances in Minnesota, about 28 to 29 minutes a night.
His usage should drop next to Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball and Jaden McDaniels, but stay above 20.

Experts call him overvalued at a price near rank 50. He is not a round 4 player, and his drop in efficiency should stick because he will not play close enough to the basket to get his FG% and blocks back.
Minnesota has a two-game week in the matchup that starts March 15, which falls inside our fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: He is a scorer and does little else. He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues.
He is poor in steals, blocks and assists and is not a strong rebounder.
FT% is his clear weak category. He also sometimes struggles with three-point percentage.
One expert does not like him as a player and thinks he is lazy on defense.

note: The market has cooled on him: Yahoo has him at rank 129 for about 1 USD and ESPN at rank 185, which puts him at or below the last of our 144 roster spots. He cost 1 USD in our auction last season. In 9-cat he is a points-first forward with a clear FT% drag and weak defensive stats, so he fits only a punt FT% team that needs scoring, and Minnesota's two-game week in our playoffs lowers his value further. He is a 1 USD bench pick at most. Early in the season, check whether he keeps the starting job and the 28 or so minutes that ESPN's bigger projection (15.1 points) depends on.
